not-versus-still choice of any/some at a shared verb token
polarity held across a modal and a perfect construction
decision_changed: A recovering site gives the corpus a licensing variable to set against its obligation variables. A capability stop would say GPT-2 small does not track clause polarity to the determiner, which would itself be worth recording since the minimal pair is one token.
novelty_delta: Thirteenth behaviour. Prior-art search returns 0 events for polarity, negation, any and some. This is the corpus's first LICENSING relation as opposed to an obligation: 'not' does not force ' any' the way 'more' forces ' than', it makes it available, and the positive counterpart 'still' leaves ' some' as the natural continuation. Recipient and donor are a minimal pair differing in exactly one word (not versus still) and ending on the same verb token. A2 re-expresses the variable in a perfect construction. The control is same-answer under two verbs that both take ' some' with no polarity item involved.
